newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: MALBAK SAYS UNBUNDLING TO ADD 15 PCT VALUE.
newsitem.headline: MALBAK SAYS UNBUNDLING TO ADD 15 PCT VALUE.

text.p: South African conglomerate Malbak Ltd said on Monday its planned unbundling could add 15 percent in value for shareholders.
Acting chief executive Peter Beningfield said shareholders were likely to receive shares in the listed companies controlled by the company plus a cash payment for the unlisted entities.

On Friday's closing prices and valuations for the unlisted companies, professional advisers valued Malbak assets at 24.60 a share, he said. Malbak shares closed at 21.50 rand on Monday, up from 21.35 on Friday.

Beningfield said the indicative prices received for certain listed companies -- Foodcorp , Kohler , South African Druggists , Ellerine and New Clicks -- did not reflect the value they could receive after unbundling.
As a result the shares were likely to be distributed to Malbak shareholders.
"This, however, does not exclude the possibility of a full value offer being received and referred to shareholders," he said.
Malbak has invited those interested in bidding for its various investments to submit indicative offers by November 29. The target date for completion of the unbundling remains end of March 1997.

Beningfield said negotiations were in progress for the sale of the unlisted subsidiaries -- including Malbak Motor Holdings, Defy, Eagle Freight, ICL (SA), Teledex and Amalgamated Appliances -- but no agreements had yet been finalised.
The most likely scenario for the unbundling was for the unlisted companies to be sold, the majority for cash, with the proceeds distributed to shareholders.
"If a new listing of any company would create more wealth for shareholders then this route will be followed and, of course, these shares distributed to Malbak shareholders," Beningfield said.
Malbak noted that the Sanlam/Rembrandt grouping held over 35 percent of the shares in Foodcorp, Kohler, SA Druggists and Ellerine.

Where practical -- and with the possible exception of SA Druggists -- this grouping aimed to sell control of their strategic stakes in the listed companies in a single transaction to secure a control premium, Beningfield said.
Due to exchange controls, Malbak's shares in London-listed MY Holdings cannot be distributed to shareholders and the company will be treated as an unlisted unit.
